title: Simplify asset pipeline: canonical shard index and decouple tokenizer handoff
creator: Ava Chen
description: The current model asset ingestion pipeline contains multiple ad-hoc weight index formats, inconsistent shard numbering conventions, and a tokenizer handoff that mixes byte-level and token-level responsibilities. This ticket aims to rationalize the on-disk weight index into a canonical shard index, introduce a small stable loader contract for streaming shards, and separate tokenizer I/O responsibilities to remove order-dependent hacks. The goal is reduced runtime branching, fewer cold-path allocations, and clearer upgrade paths for new checkpoint formats.
background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated three competing weight manifest variants and two different shard ID schemes used by different model importers. Runtime code has grown checks for legacy formats, which affects cold-start latency and increases complexity when adding quantized variant support. Tokenizer integration currently happens during model bootstrap which couples disk IO to tokenizer initialization and prevents parallelization of shard streaming and tokenizer tokenization in some private deploy paths.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a small canonical shard-index schema (json lines) that maps stable shard_id -> byte ranges + checksum + format-tag. 2) Add a thin loader adapter that can emit streamable shard descriptors and supports a fallback compatibility layer for legacy manifests. 3) Extract tokenizer initialization into a separate stage with a clear async contract: tokenizer.prepare(metadata) -> tokenizer.ready future, and a tokenizer.bind_io(loader) step for runtime that only attaches when needed. 4) Migrate model ingesters to emit canonical manifests as part of the ingestion pipeline and add a compatibility-conversion tool for existing buckets. 5) Add unit tests, an end-to-end integration test that validates a reference model (gptx-2B) loads in < 1s cold start on CI, and perf benchmarks to measure improved startup and lower allocations.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical shard-index schema documented and spec committed in repo: docs/shard-index.md
Loader adapter implemented with a clear streaming API and a compatibility fallback for legacy manifests
Tokenizer init extracted: tokenizer.prepare(...) returns a future and no longer performs blocking disk reads during model bootstrap
End-to-end tests added that validate correctness across three existing checkpoint formats
Cold-start time for reference model reduced by >= 10% in CI microbenchmark
Migration tool created to convert existing manifests to canonical format and a one-off migration plan drafted for Dedicated customers

progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Initial schema draft posted to PR #5482; reviewed by @maria and @raj. Key decision: use newline-delimited JSON for streaming friendliness.
2025-01-20: Prototype loader adapter implemented; passes unit tests for two legacy manifests. Observed ~12% reduction in peak allocations when using streaming path locally.
2025-01-28: Tokenizer init contract proposed. We decoupled byte-level vocab reads from model weight reads; still evaluating edge-case for sentencepiece models with external merges files.
2025-02-02: Migration tool spike completed; conversion time for 50GB model artifacts ~4.3 minutes on staging runner. Preparing canary migration run for staging-Dedicated cluster next week.
notes: Trade-offs: newline-delimited JSON is heavier than binary manifest but simplifies incremental parsing and human debugging.
We considered protobuf manifests for size but decided against for backwards-compatible streaming readability.
Edge-case: models that interleave tokenizer vocab in separate archive files require a small 'auxiliary_files' field in the canonical manifest; added to schema proposal.
Operational: add migration-run tagging so Dedicated customers can opt into a staged convert; do not perform in-place conversions without approval.
Benchmark: early local runs show 8-14% cold-start improvement on p3.2xlarge-like nodes; need CI validation on our sanctioned machines.
